question: Should Microsoft Teams adopt `channels.msteams.accounts` plus `defaultAccount`, preserve root-level configuration as the implicit default account, and require a separate webhook port for each named bot?
rationale: The code is credible and well-proven, but this creates a durable public configuration, inheritance, deployment, authentication, and state contract that requires explicit maintainer intent rather than reviewer inference.

options.title: Sponsor named accounts
options.body: Confirm the proposed account and inheritance model, then reopen or continue the implementation after narrow cleanup and upgrade proof.

options.title: Request a narrower contract
options.body: Define fewer inherited fields or a different listener topology before sponsoring implementation.

options.title: Keep single-account Teams
options.body: Decline the new public surface and retain the current one-bot-per-gateway Teams contract.

recommendation.title: Sponsor named accounts
recommendation.body: Confirm the proposed account and inheritance model, then reopen or continue the implementation after narrow cleanup and upgrade proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current-main history signal spans the central Teams configuration, monitor, channel, and setup surfaces involved in this product decision.
